evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Uncashed checks and dormant balances, tracked to each state's deadline.' plus a lede naming 'controllers and accounting managers at companies of 200 to 2,000 people, who usually meet the obligation for the first time in an audit letter'. What, who and next step ('Request an assessment call') are all stated. The lede runs to five lines at 1440 and nine at 390, so the 'who' is the last thing you read.
evidence.fit: As the controller holding an audit letter, I get a path right after the hero: 'If the audit letter has already arrived', with what the state wants, what records I need, and 'Counsel handles the audit itself'. The FAQ answers 'We have never filed. Is it too late?' with voluntary disclosure. As the CFO asking whether the process is controlled, I get the Delaware entry with statute citations, an entry log ('Second reviewer signed off'), reconciliation notes and a filing archive. The not-a-law-firm constraint shows in a red-ruled notice beside the state rules. Weakness: the artifacts are static, and the page commits to services the brief never mentions (submitting 'on your behalf', 45 minutes 'with someone who has prepared these filings', reviewer names on entries).
evidence.distinctiveness: The 'A holder's reporting year' calendar in the hero and the 'State rules / Delaware / Verified Sep 14, 2026' panel come from the product's world. The rest follows the familiar order: three numbered step columns, a dark CTA band with Bring/Leave with lists, and an FAQ accordion.
evidence.proof: The hero diagram is a static calendar of deadlines, labelled 'This diagram is illustrative', and does not show my items being tracked. The Delaware state entry (about screen 3) and the 'Fall 2026' filing summary (about screen 4) are static. The filing summary contradicts itself: the header says 'Cutoff June 30, 2026', yet its Texas row is 'Filed' and due 'Jul 1, 2026', and Delaware is due Mar 1, 2027 inside the same 'Fall 2026' cycle. A controller would spot this.
evidence.craft: 1440: the hero copy column takes the left half and the right half is an empty patterned field until the diagram starts at about y=680. That is a large dead area in the first screen. Type is a calm serif and spacing is even. 390: the filing summary table is clipped after 'Notices sent', so Due and Status are only reachable by swiping inside the panel (probe axe: scrollable-region-focusable).
evidence.mobile: 390: the hero stacks, both buttons are full width at about 45px, and the calendar is recomposed as a vertical list ('Mar 1 Delaware' ... 'Nov 1 Most other states'). The Menu toggle opens a full list that includes the CTA, label changes to 'Close', Escape closes it, and tapping 'State rules' closes it and scrolls. Weaknesses: the filing ledger's Due/Status columns sit off the right edge, the first screen at 390 has no artifact (the calendar starts at y=719), and the page is about 8,700px long.
evidence.honesty: Examples are labelled where they appear: 'This diagram is illustrative', 'Preview of a state entry. Values are a snapshot taken for this page', 'Example filing summary with placeholder figures'. 'We are early. We do not yet have customer logos or audit outcomes to show, and we will not invent them' is plain. Several operational promises are not in the brief and are stated as fact: a second reviewer signs off every entry, reviewer names on each entry, filing on the customer's behalf, a 45-minute call, written estimate and 'plain price for the year'.
evidence.interaction: The only controls are the menu and the FAQ. 1440: I clicked all six <summary> items and every one opened. 390: Menu toggled, aria-expanded flipped, Escape closed it and returned focus, and a link click closed it. Tab order runs skip link, brand, nav, CTA, secondary, all with a 3px outline. No console errors. There is no demo or artifact to operate, so nothing shows the product responding to input.
evidence.copy: Specific and from the controller's world: 'an audit firm working for several states on a contingent fee', 'Gaps in the records are usually filled by estimate, which rarely favors the holder', 'voided, reissued and cashed items drop off with a note of why'. Button labels say what happens. The hero lede and the step paragraphs run long, and the 'Leave with' list reads like a sales promise.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, named audience and CTA, with the top half of the illustrative calendar visible at the bottom. The calendar shows that deadlines vary, not that Holdfast tracks my checks. 390: headline, a nine-line lede and two buttons fill the viewport, with nothing in view that backs the promise.

problems: No operable or item-level artifact: the product's core job (my checks → state → deadline) is never shown, only a static illustrative calendar and later static tables

The example filing summary is internally inconsistent (Texas filed Jul 1, 2026 under a 'Cutoff June 30, 2026' Fall cycle), which is exactly what a careful controller or CFO would catch on a page selling deadline accuracy

The page promises services and controls the brief does not supply (second-reviewer sign-off, filing on the customer's behalf, 45 minutes with someone who has prepared filings), and the 1440 hero has a large empty right half

evidence.clarity: H1 'Every stale check has a state deadline.' plus 'Holdfast is unclaimed property software for finance teams. It tracks uncashed checks and dormant customer balances, works out which state each one belongs to and when it is due, and prepares the report that state requires.' What it does and the next step are clear at 1440 and 390. The audience reads as 'finance teams' until the 'Built for' block near the end, where it narrows to 'Controllers and accounting managers at companies with 200 to 2,000 employees'.
evidence.fit: The hero register is the controller's own artefact: the outstanding-check list from a bank rec, re-sorted 'As Holdfast files it' into Past due / Report to California by Nov 1, 2026 / Clock still running. The CTA is the brief's URL, and 'The call is free. Bring your outstanding-check list' sets expectations. The legal constraint appears beside every sample ('Not legal advice', 'Confirm dates with your counsel'). 'Built for / Not for' is a good filter. Weaker for the CFO and auditor: the audit letter is mentioned only in the call section, there is nothing on voluntary disclosure or lookback, and the controls story is limited to 'last checked' dates and 'the summary your auditor will ask for'.
evidence.distinctiveness: Structure comes from the product. A sample register is toggled between bank-rec order and filing order, then one check (10492) is followed through five dates (issued, stale, dormant, letter, report), and the California report is built from check 10517 of the same list. Monospaced data type and ledger chips look like a finance tool, not a startup template.
evidence.proof: 1440: the operable register with Ashby Tool & Die sample data sits beside the headline in the first screen. Numbers are consistent across sections: 12 checks · $10,318.39 overall; the summary (2 past due $499.15; next filing California Nov 1, 2026 · $2,310.00; 8 running $6,225.24) matches the groups; check 10492's Texas dates (dormant Apr 14, 2026, report Jul 1, 2027) match the timeline; check 10517 is the only item in the California report. 'sample data' is printed in the register header.
evidence.craft: Clear hierarchy with a heavy serif display and mono data. Status colour (red past due, green due) carries meaning and has text with it. Minor defects at 1440: the rules table's footnote leaves a white gap beside it, the register tfoot grey bar stops short, and the register runs to about y=1515, so the left column is empty below the summary. 390: the rules table shows only State/Dormancy/Period ends, with Report due and Last checked off to the right, and the report table cuts 'PROPERT…'.
evidence.mobile: 390: the register is recomposed into stacked cards (payee, amount, state, dormant date, deadline chip). Segmented control labels are 50px tall, inputs and Reset are 44px, and the error message appears directly above the list. The hero summary (Past due / Next filing / Still on the clock) is in the first screen and the register starts at y=791. Menu opens and closes with Escape and on link tap, but holds only three section links and no CTA, and the header CTA is hidden at 390. The rules table hides 'Report due' behind a sideways swipe with no cue.
evidence.honesty: Samples are labelled where they sit: 'Ashby Tool & Die, Inc. · sample data', 'Sample check, sample payee. Not legal advice', 'Sample: eight of the states Holdfast covers, for vendor checks only', 'Illustrative. Names, addresses and amounts are sample data'. No logos or quotes. Small unsupported claims: 'The call is free' and 'pricing is quoted ... by number of legal entities' are not in the brief, and every rule row shows 'Last checked Oct 20, 2026', which reads as a verification claim even though the table is labelled a sample.
evidence.interaction: 1440 and 390: switching to 'As your bank rec lists it' re-renders by check number with Date/Address state columns. Setting incorporation to 'Another state' moved the two unaddressed checks into 'State not in this eight-state sample · 2 checks $775.00' and updated 'Still on the clock' to 6 checks. As-of 2028-01-15 regrouped the list to 5 past due and next filing 'Illinois, May 1, 2028 · 107 days'. Clearing the date showed 'No date entered, so the list is shown as of Jan 15, 2028.' 2040-01-01 showed 'Pick a date between Jan 1, 2020 and Dec 31, 2035 ...' in red above the list. 'Reset sample' restored Oct 20, 2026 / Delaware. Radios respond to arrow keys, a polite live region announces each change, and there were no console errors.
evidence.copy: Written in the controller's language: 'Writing it back to income is the entry auditors look for first', 'Status: outstanding 6 months · do not write off', 'the report is a list to confirm rather than a search to start', 'The assessment call starts from your check list, not a demo.' Error messages are written, not defaulted. Terms (dormant, cutoff, report, notice) are used consistently.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, CTA with what-to-bring microcopy, a sample summary and the operable register with real-looking checks grouped by state deadline, labelled sample, all in one viewport. 390: headline, subhead, CTA, call microcopy and the sample summary (2 past due, California Nov 1) are in view. The register itself starts just below the fold, and the audience is 'finance teams' rather than controllers.

problems: The CFO and auditor readers get no dedicated path: no audit-letter section near the top, nothing on voluntary disclosure or lookback, and statute sources are promised 'in the product' rather than shown
390: the rules table hides 'Report due' and 'Last checked' behind an unhinted sideways swipe, the report table clips its columns, and the mobile menu has no CTA
Small unsupported specifics ('The call is free', pricing 'by number of legal entities', every rule row 'Last checked Oct 20, 2026') that the founder would have to stand behind

reason: As a controller arriving cold, B is the only page that shows the product doing my job: my kind of check list re-sorted into past due, next filing and still running, with consistent numbers carried through to the timeline and the report, and every sample labelled. A speaks better to the audit-letter moment and to a CFO's control questions (entry log, statute citations, voluntary disclosure FAQ), but it shows nothing operable, its example ledger contradicts itself on dates, and it promises services the brief doesn't support. I would switch to A if the CFO and auditor reading were weighted above the controller's first-screen proof.
